items.title: What Was Cisco Telling You Before Its Stock Ran?
items.summary: Cisco Systems (CSCO) stock returned 62% in the twelve months to September 24, 2026, against 16% for the S&P 500. A $10,000 holding at the start was worth about $16,220 at the end. The run was about AI data center orders from hyperscalers, the largest cloud companies. You could have read the run early only if two things held: Cisco was saying it, and its results were showing it.

items.title: These Tech Stocks Trade Near Buy Points. One Sees 80% To 100% Core Income Growth.
items.summary: The technology sector led the stock market's gains this week, with three tech names making new highs.

items.title: Dell Rises 7% as Morgan Stanley Lifts Odds on $756 Bull Case; Hewlett Packard Enterprise Edges Higher
items.summary: Morgan Stanley raised the odds on a scenario that would send Dell far beyond its current price, yet the firm kept its rating neutral and its base case unchanged. That contradiction is exactly what buyers are betting on today.

items.title: 2 Growth Stocks with All-Star Potential and 1 We Find Risky
items.summary: Growth boosts valuation multiples, but it doesn’t always last forever. Companies that cannot maintain it are often penalized with large declines in market value, a lesson ingrained in investors who lost money in tech stocks during 2022.

items.title: NVIDIA’s Next AI Chip Ramp Could Open the Door to Another Major Stock Move
items.summary: NVIDIA's forecast to double chip volume, near-unanimous analyst Buy ratings, and rising price targets underscore a bullish outlook, with OEMs like Dell and HPE also poised to benefit.

items.title: Super Micro’s Vera Rubin Shipments Put Its AI Infrastructure Advantage to the Test
items.summary: Super Micro Computer shipped NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 liquid-cooled racks, backed by a $60 billion backlog, even as its forward P/E of 10.26 remains low ahead of November earnings.
